messages:
Alex Chen: main turned red immediately after merging my PR. Failing stage: gpu-e2e -> serve_runtime/cache_integration_test. @Priya Nair can you take a look? I didn't see failures in my local runs.

Infra Bot: Pipeline #4827 failed
Stage: gpu-e2e
Task: serve_runtime_tests
Exit: 1
Logs snippet:
```
E tensorflow: cuda runtime error: out of memory
[2027-07-01T12:34:56Z] worker gpu-003-east: kernel: oom_reaper invoked
```

Priya Nair: On it. Kicking off a rerun now. Will check node logs and allocator traces. :eyes:

Jordan Lee: fwiw we merged allocator changes in PR #4100 yesterday. Could be related to fragmentation.

Sam QA: I reproduced locally on a T4 VM — test times out during kv-cache warmup at ~12s, then OOM on a subsequent op. Saving logs.

Priya Nair: Rerun started: https://ci.redwood/4827/rerun. If rerun passes, likely flake; if not we bisect.

Infra Bot: Rerun result: gpu-e2e passed on second attempt on node gpu-001-west. Original failure node: gpu-003-east still shows kernel OOMs.

Priya Nair: Hmm, inconsistent. Spawning a bisect job across commits (PR #4100..HEAD) to see regression point.

Alex Chen: If allocator change is the suspect, can we try pinning runtime to previous allocator patch for the Dedicated pool? Otherwise I'll revert my merge to stabilize main.

Jordan Lee: I can try a targeted revert of PR #4100 on a branch and run the failing test across nodes.

Sam QA: Filing follow-up ticket ENG-INFRA-223 with logs and repro steps. Adding 'flaky' label to the test for now.

Priya Nair: Update: bisect points to commit a9f7c2 (allocator pool refactor). Opening a PR to adjust pool behavior and add a test that reproduces fragmentation locally.

Alex Chen: Going to revert my merge to be safe. Reverted commit 7c5d9f on main. Rerunning main pipeline.

Infra Bot: Main pipeline #4829 after revert: all green.

Alex Chen: Main is green after revert. Thanks everyone for the quick triage. We'll follow up on ENG-INFRA-223. :thumbsup:
